newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dorbyl sees 55-60mln rand loss from project.
newsitem.headline: Dorbyl sees 55-60mln rand loss from project.

text.p: Engineering group Dorbyl Ltd said on Tuesday it would incur losses of between 55 and 60 million rand in the Intershore joint venture and would withdraw from the project in April this year.
The company said in a statement, however, that the losses would have no material impact on earnings per share for the year to March 31 as they had been largely offset by non-trading profits.
The Intershore project -- a joint venture between Dorbyl, Murray & Roberts and British firm Amec plc -- was awarded a contract to build two oil platforms in Cabinda, Angola in early 1994.
"The decision to exit this business, together with shipbuilding, was taken in 1995, but the contract had to be completed before Dorbyl could withdraw from Intershore," it said.
The completion date for the entire project was estimated to be mid-April 1997.
The company said its withdrawal from the project would mark the last major step in its transformation to a manufacturing and distribution company from a heavy engineering and contracting firm.
